note: Michael's FCE Writing Portfolio (2026 slides), transcribed slide for slide. Each structure = three bands: Introduction (A | B), Arguments (P), Conclusion (P). Item prefixes: '> ' sub-bullet, '## ' heading inside a column, '= ' bold line with no bullet (a greeting), '! ' italic note, '**…**' bold. ' || ' puts a grey aside at the end of a line. Model plans: '### ' heading line, '• ' bullet, '**…**' bold. Typos fixed against the PDF are listed in 'fixes'. The Story structure is NOT in the portfolio: it is a draft in the same shape.

Opinion model: 'I am convince that' → 'I am convinced that'
Formal emails: 'Dear Sir,' → 'Dear Sir or Madam,' (as in the models)
Review: 'This is a …. Which' → 'This is a … which'; '….. Is a must' → '… is a must'; 'of …. Is …' → 'of … is …'

plan: **Is it better to earn a lot of money or to enjoy your job?**
### High income – advantages
• provides financial security and stability
• allows comfortable lifestyle and reduces stress
### Job satisfaction – advantages:
• increases productivity and wellbeing
• contributes to lasting happiness
### Balanced perspective (your own idea):
• long-term happiness depends on meaningful work
• wealth helps but cannot replace fulfilment
text: **Few people would deny that** job satisfaction and financial stability are both essential aspects of modern life. In recent years, the question of whether it is better to earn a lot of money or to enjoy your job has sparked considerable debate. Therefore, it is vital to analyse the advantages and disadvantages of both options before reaching a conclusion.

**The main advantage of earning a high income is that** it provides a sense of security. For instance, financial stability allows people to pay bills comfortably and enjoy a better lifestyle. Supporters of this view often point out that a reliable income reduces stress and gives a feeling of control.

**On the other hand, many argue that** enjoying work is more important than earning large sums. People who love what they do tend to be more productive and experience greater well-being. As a result, job satisfaction often contributes to lasting happiness.
**Another important point is that** long-term happiness depends on doing meaningful work. Wealth helps, but it cannot replace fulfilment.
In conclusion, both money and job satisfaction **have advantages and disadvantages**. On balance, genuine happiness arises from work that provides purpose as well as comfort.

plan: **Some people prefer to study abroad, while others choose to study in their own country.**
### International experience
• provides international experience and language practice
• develops independence, confidence and open-mindedness
### Challenges
• expensive, emotionally demanding
• homesickness, isolation, cultural challenges
### Benefits
• more affordable and familiar
• family support and local connections offer stability
text: **Over the past decade**, more students have chosen to study abroad. It is widely recognised that this experience offers valuable opportunities but also presents challenges. Hence, it is important to consider the advantages and disadvantages of studying abroad compared with staying in one’s home country.

**The main argument in favour of s**tudying abroad is that it provides international experience. Students can learn new languages, adapt to different cultures and gain independence. Consequently, they often become more open-minded and confident.

**Nevertheless, the key disadvantage of studying abroad is that** it can be expensive and emotionally demanding. Tuition fees and living costs are higher than at home, and some students may feel homesick or isolated. Despite these issues, many believe such experiences help young people grow personally and professionally.

**A clear advantage of staying** in one’s own country is that it is more affordable and familiar. Moreover, students can rely on family support and local connections, which often help them stay focused and comfortable while studying.
**Overall, while both options have benefits and drawbacks**, the experience of living abroad can ultimately be seen as both enriching and challenging.

plan: **What are the causes of pollution and how can we solve them?**
### Solutions (government level):
• Stricter regulations and renewable energy
• Authorities introduce environmental policies
### Solutions (alternative transport)
• public transport
• Cycling
### Solutions (individual level):
• Use public transport, recycle, reduce emissions
• Public awareness campaigns
text: **Across the world, pollution has become a serious problem that affects** everyone’s health and the environment. Few people would deny that we need to act now to reduce pollution. Hence, it is vital to examine practical solutions and discuss how this problem can be solved.

**One possible solution to this problem would be to** make stricter rules about pollution from factories. Governments could introduce policies that stop companies from releasing harmful smoke and chemicals. For instance, if factories had to pay fines when they polluted too much, they would use clean energy like solar or wind power. As this measure develops, the air would get cleaner and greenhouse gases would go down.

**A practical way to address this issue is by** making public transport better and encouraging cycling instead of driving. Authorities could introduce policies such as cheaper buses and trains, and safe bike lanes in cities. If current transport patterns shift towards greener options, pollution from cars would be reduced. By taking these steps, cities could reduce the damage caused by traffic.

**Individuals can also play a role by** making eco-friendly choices every day. People should be encouraged to recycle, use less electricity, and buy products with less packaging. Furthermore, public awareness campaigns could help to teach everyone why protecting nature matters. Even small changes can make a real difference.

To sum up, a combination of government rules, better transport, and personal responsibility is needed to fight pollution. On balance, it seems clear **that solving environmental problems needs everyone to work together**.

plan: **What are the main causes of traffic problems in cities, and how can they be solved?**
### Solutions (alternative transport)
• improve buses and trains
• making public transport more reliable
### Solutions (introducing better laws)
• flexible timetable
• plan better neighbourhood
### Solutions (individual level):
• Promote shared or electric transport
• Car-sharing schemes, walking, cycling
text: **In major cities worldwide, traffic congestion has become increasingly serious**, causing delays, pollution, and stress. It is widely recognised that this problem affects both work and wellbeing. Therefore, it is essential that we look into effective solutions and consider how they might help.

**An effective measure could be to** improve buses and trains and create safer bike paths. The government should take steps to make public transport more reliable and affordable so people don’t need to drive everywhere. Authorities could introduce policies such as building new metro lines and protected cycling lanes. Should this approach be implemented, roads would be less crowded and the air would be cleaner.

**Another practical solution involves** changing how and when people work. Companies could offer flexible hours or let employees work from home sometimes to avoid rush hour. Furthermore, city planners should design neighbourhoods where shops are close by, so people can walk. These actions would help reduce unnecessary car trips.

**It is essential for governments to implement measures to** promote car-sharing and discourage everyone driving alone. People should be encouraged to adopt other ways of getting around, like walking or cycling. Public awareness campaigns could help to change attitudes about transport.

Overall, while traffic problems cannot be solved overnight, consistent efforts can lead to real progress. In conclusion, **the most effective strategy involves** governments, businesses, and ordinary people all working together.

plan: **What are the main causes and effects of obesity today?**
### Causes of obesity:
• unhealthy diet – too much fast food, sugar and processed meals
• lack of exercise due to modern lifestyles and technology
### Effects on individuals:
• health problems – diabetes, heart disease, joint pain
• emotional issues – low self-esteem and depression
### Social effects (your own idea):
• higher healthcare costs and lower productivity
• governments need education and prevention programmes
text: Obesity **has become one of the fastest-growing health concerns** worldwide. Therefore, it is essential to examine the main causes and the resulting effects.
**One major cause of obesity is that** people consume too much fast food. For example, many rely on cheap, processed meals. As a result, calorie intake is high while nutrition is poor.
**Another reason is that lifestyles are increasingly** sedentary. For instance, many spend long hours sitting at computers. Consequently, energy is not burned, leading to weight gain.

**The effects of these habits can be seen** in rising health problems. In particular, obesity increases the risk of diabetes and heart disease. Compared with previous generations, today’s population faces far more medical complications.
**In conclusion, obesity results mainly from** unhealthy diets and lack of exercise. On balance, prevention through education and lifestyle change is the best solution.

plan: **Why are so many people moving to large cities, and what results does this have?**
### Paragraph 2 – Causes of urban migration
• Better job opportunities and higher salaries
• Access to education, healthcare, and entertainment
### Paragraph 3 – Positive effects
• Economic growth and cultural diversity
• Cities attract skilled workers and innovation
### Paragraph 4 – Negative effects (own idea)
• Overcrowding, traffic, and pollution increase
• High living costs and housing shortages
text: **Driven by jobs and services,** millions are moving to cities, with mixed results. Hence, this essay will discuss the causes of this movement and its main effects.
**One of the main reasons is that** cities offer better job opportunities. For example, young people move to find stable employment. As a result, urban populations grow rapidly.

**Another key cause lies in** the availability of education and healthcare. This attracts families seeking better futures for their children. However, overcrowding soon becomes a serious problem. The effects of this migration are evident in housing shortages and higher living costs.
In addition, traffic and pollution levels increase. Consequently, city life **becomes** stressful and unhealthy, which **can lead to** other concerning issues.

In conclusion, urban migration **is caused by** economic and social factors but also creates new difficulties. Therefore, governments should invest in regional development to balance population growth.

plan: **Children should start school at a younger age. Do you agree?**
• **learning habits** (Paragraph 2 – argues that starting early helps children learn basic skills and develop social habits sooner)
• loss of **playtime** (Paragraph 3 – explains that it may cause stress and reduce time for play and creativity)
• **your opinion** (Paragraph 4 – own idea; supports starting school at a reasonable age but keeping a balance between learning and play)
text: **Nowadays, there is debate about** the best age for children to begin school. Therefore, this essay will examine both sides before giving a personal opinion.

**One strong argument in favour of** early schooling is that it encourages learning habits. For instance, children who start young may develop stronger literacy skills. As a result, they are more confident later in education.

However, **the main argument against** starting too early is that young children need more playtime. For example, long classroom hours can cause stress. Consequently, motivation to learn may decrease.
**Although both views have merit**, I believe that formal education should begin at a balanced age. In this way, children can enjoy childhood while building essential skills.
In conclusion, **while early education offers advantages**, a moderate starting age ensures healthy development and lifelong learning enthusiasm.

plan: **Advertising is more harmful than useful. Do you agree?**
• **informs and entertains** (Paragraph 2 – argues ads give information and fund media)
• **creates false needs** (Paragraph 3 – criticises manipulation and consumerism)
• **balance** (Paragraph 4 – own idea; supports responsible regulation)
text: **Nowadays, advertising plays a powerful role in our daily lives**. Consequently, it is essential to discuss whether it influences people unfairly.

Those who **agree tend to argue that** advertisements create unnecessary desires. For example, they persuade consumers to purchase luxury products. As a result, people spend money on items they rarely use.

On the other hand**, supporters of advertising claim that** it provides information about useful goods. For instance, it helps small businesses reach potential customers. This shows that not all advertising is harmful.

Although advertising can sometimes be manipulative, **I believe that** responsibility **also lies with** consumers. If people make informed choices, they can enjoy the benefits of advertising without waste.
In conclusion, while advertising influences behaviour, self-awareness and education **are the keys to** using it wisely.

plan: **Should people spend time helping others on a regular basis?**
### Paragraph 2 – Benefits for the community
• Volunteering helps improve social life and community spirit
• Examples: food drives, charity events, neighbourhood projects
### Paragraph 3 – Benefits for the volunteer
• Builds empathy, teamwork, and self-confidence
• Reduces loneliness, increases emotional satisfaction
### Paragraph 4 – Personal view (own idea)
• Everyone can contribute in small ways
• Simple daily kindnesses make a long-term difference
text: **Helping others should be a normal part of everyday life**. I **strongly believe that** everyone should contribute regularly because it benefits both the community and the individual.

Firstly, **volunteering is an excellent way to make society better**. Taking part in local projects such as food collections, charity events or environmental clean-ups helps people in need and creates stronger communities. When citizens work together, they build trust and cooperation.

Secondly, **in my view**, helping others is also rewarding for the volunteer. It teaches empathy, develops teamwork skills, and increases confidence. Moreover, it gives a sense of purpose and emotional satisfaction that money can’t buy.
Finally, **I am convinced that** even small acts of kindness can have a big effect. Smiling at someone, helping a neighbour, or giving up time for a good cause can inspire others to do the same.
In conclusion, **helping others benefits both sides** — those who give and those who receive. To sum up, kindness should become part of everyone’s daily routine.

plan: **Do people rely too much on technology nowadays?**
### Paragraph 2 – Convenience and benefits
• Technology makes tasks faster and easier
• Examples – online shopping, digital communication, apps
• However, too much convenience can reduce independence
### Paragraph 3 – Negative effects on people
• Overuse leads to lack of real-life interaction
• Families spend less time talking face-to-face
• Dependence causes laziness and distraction
### Paragraph 4 – Finding balance (own idea)
• Technology should support, not replace, human activity
• Learning to disconnect improves focus and relationships
text: **From work to free time,** digital tools guide daily life — perhaps a little too much. However, I firmly believe that society depends on it excessively.

**To begin with, the main reason for** this dependence **is that** digital tools make everything easier. For instance, people use apps even for simple tasks. As a result, they lose basic problem-solving skills.

**Another argument supporting this view is that** technology affects relationships. For example, families often spend evenings staring at screens. Consequently, face-to-face communication is declining.
**Nevertheless, it is true that** technology brings comfort and efficiency. Yet, over-reliance can cause isolation and laziness.
In conclusion, while technology **offers clear benefits**, we should limit its use to maintain real-world skills and personal connections.

plan: **How will technology change the way we work in the next twenty years?**
### Scientific discoveries + Space travel accessibility
• Research leads to major discoveries
• New materials and energy sources
### International competition + Colonization
• Nations competing for prestige
• Heavy government investment
### Criticism about priorities
• Ambitions unrealistic
• Poverty and climate change unsolved
text: **In recent years, space exploration has become one of the most exciting** and controversial areas of science. Many experts predict that this field will continue to expand rapidly in the decades to come.

**It is widely believed that research beyond Earth will lead to** major discoveries. Scientists may soon find new materials or forms of energy that could transform life on our planet. Space travel is also expected to become more common as technology develops and costs fall.

**At the same time, it is likely that** competition among nations will intensify. Governments might invest heavily in space projects to gain international prestige. In the long term, this could result in colonies on the Moon or even Mars.

**Nevertheless, some people argue that s**uch ambitions are unrealistic while poverty and climate change remain unsolved. Unless world priorities change, investment in space may face criticism for ignoring urgent human problems.

**In conclusion, space exploration will probably remain** an important symbol of human progress. However, its future success is likely to depend on how well science serves the needs of our own planet.

plan: **What will schools be like in 100 years?**
• **technology in classrooms** (Paragraph 2 – AI teachers, virtual reality, flexible online lessons, textbooks disappear)
• **learning skills** (Paragraph 3 – creativity, teamwork, problem-solving replace memorising facts and exams)
• **social development (your own idea)** (Paragraph 4 – schools still need human teachers for empathy, motivation, and cooperation)
text: **Nowadays, education is undergoing a remarkable transformation**. Over the past few years, there has been a growing trend towards digital learning and flexible study methods. Therefore, it is important to consider what schools might look like in the future and how teaching could continue to evolve.

**It is likely that technology will keep reshaping the way** students learn. Lessons will probably become even more interactive, with artificial intelligence helping teachers to adapt materials to individual needs. Virtual reality could allow learners to experience subjects in realistic environments, and traditional textbooks may soon disappear.

**If current patterns persist, schools will focus more on** creativity, teamwork and problem-solving rather than memorising facts. Students might work on real-life projects and use technology to address global challenges.
**Despite these changes, schools will still need to provide** social and emotional support. Human contact between students and teachers will remain essential.
**In conclusion, the trend towards digital and flexible learning will continue to expand**, but the school of the future will always depend on human connection as well as innovation.

plan: ### Eating habits
• Mention common problems – junk food, skipping meals
• Suggest eating fruit, vegetables, and drinking water regularly
• Share quick meal ideas for busy students
### Exercise and daily routine
• Recommend walking or cycling to school
• Include short workouts or sports with friends
• Explain benefits – more energy and better mood
### Mental health (own idea)
• Take breaks, get enough sleep, talk to others when stressed
• Balance study with hobbies and relaxation
text: Are you finding it hard to stay healthy while studying? Between classes, homework, and social life, it’s easy to forget about fitness. However, a few small changes can make a big difference.

First of all, try to eat proper meals instead of relying on snacks or fast food. Fruit, vegetables, and plenty of water will give you the energy you need to concentrate. If you often skip breakfast, prepare something simple like fruit and yoghurt the night before.

Exercise is just as important. You don’t have to join a gym — walking or cycling to school and taking the stairs can help you stay fit. Playing sports with friends is not only good for your body but also for your mood.
Finally, don’t forget your mental health. Take regular breaks, get enough sleep, and make time to relax or talk to someone if you’re stressed.
In short, staying healthy as a student isn’t difficult if you plan your time well. Why not start today?

plan: ### What to do there
• Describe main attractions or activities – sightseeing, food, events
• Explain what makes it special or different from other places
### Personal experience
• Mention a favourite memory or something enjoyable from your visit
• Use descriptive language and sensory details
### Practical tips (own idea)
• Best time to visit, where to stay, how to get there cheaply
• Advice for families, couples, or students
text: If you’re looking for the perfect place to spend a weekend, you should definitely visit **Sintra**, a beautiful town just outside Lisbon. It’s full of charm, history, and breath-taking scenery.

There’s so much to see and do. You can explore colourful palaces, wander through green forests, or relax in cosy cafés. The views from the hills are stunning, especially from the famous *Pena Palace*. Don’t forget your camera!
When I visited last spring, I loved walking through the narrow streets and tasting local pastries. Everything felt calm and friendly, far from the stress of city life.
If you plan to go, it’s best to visit in spring or autumn, when the weather is warm but not too hot. Trains from Lisbon are cheap and frequent, which makes travelling there easy.
All in all, Sintra is a magical weekend destination. I’d recommend it to anyone who enjoys nature, history, and delicious food — you’ll definitely want to go back!

plan: ### Opening (Greeting & Purpose)
• Begin formally: *Dear Sir or Madam,*
• State reason for writing – applying for advertised summer job
• Mention where you saw the advert
### Paragraph 1 – Experience and skills
• Describe relevant experience (working with people, languages, tourism)
• Mention positive qualities – responsible, hardworking, enthusiastic
### Paragraph 2 – Request for information
• Ask about working hours, accommodation, and salary
• Clarify start and end dates if necessary
text: **Dear Sir or Madam,**
I am writing to apply for the summer position advertised on your website. I am a 19-year-old student studying Tourism, and I believe I would be a suitable candidate for this job.

I have previous experience working with the public in a small café, where I developed excellent communication and teamwork skills. I speak English, Portuguese, and basic French, which I think would be useful when dealing with international guests.
I consider myself responsible, friendly, and hardworking.
I would be grateful if you could provide more details about working hours, accommodation, and salary. I am available from the beginning of July until the end of September.
Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to hearing from you soon.
Yours faithfully,
Ana Silva

text: **Dear Sir or Madam,**
I am writing to enquire about the summer English course recently advertised on your website. I would be grateful if you could provide me with further information before I apply.

Firstly, I would like to know what type of accommodation is available. Could you please tell me whether students stay with host families or in college residences? In addition, I would appreciate details regarding the facilities included, such as meals and laundry service.
Secondly, I am interested in the leisure activities offered. Are there any organised trips or sports events during the course? It would be helpful to know the typical weekly timetable.
Finally, I would like to ask how to apply and if there is a specific closing date for registration. I am planning to attend in July, so I would be grateful for a quick reply.
Thank you very much for your assistance. I look forward to hearing from you soon.
**Yours faithfully,**
Daniel Carter

plan: ### Opening (Greeting & Purpose)
• Begin informally: *Hi Alex,* or *Hey Sarah,*
• Ask how your friend is and say why you’re writing (to invite them to visit)
### Paragraph 1 – Describe your new city
• Mention what you like about it – friendly people, nice parks, cafés
• Include some details about where you live now
### Paragraph 2 – Plans for the visit
• Suggest things to do – sightseeing, concerts, restaurants
• Mention local events or your favourite places
### Paragraph 3 – Practical details (own idea)
• Offer accommodation or help with travel
• Suggest best time to come or what to bring
text: Hi Sarah,
How are you? I hope everything’s going well with your studies. I’m writing because I’ve just moved to Porto, and I’d love you to come and visit me soon!
You’d really like it here. The city is full of character, with narrow streets, amazing river views, and so many cafés and restaurants to try. My flat is near the old town, so it’s easy to get around.
If you come next month, we could go sightseeing, visit the famous wine cellars, and spend a day at the beach. There’s also a big music festival that weekend, which would be so much fun!
You can stay at my place, of course — I have a spare room. Just let me know when you’re free so I can plan everything.
Can’t wait to see you soon!
Love,
**Marta**

plan: ### Opening (Greeting & Purpose)
• Start warmly – *Hi Emily,*
• Thank them for the weekend and say you had a fantastic time
### Paragraph 1 – What you enjoyed most
• Mention specific activities – meals, trips, games, or conversations
• Describe your favourite moment briefly
### Paragraph 2 – Compliment and appreciation
• Thank them for being kind and welcoming
• Mention how comfortable or fun it was staying with them
### Paragraph 3 – Future plans (own idea)
• Suggest meeting again soon or inviting them to your place next time

text: Hi Emily,
I just wanted to say a huge thanks for last weekend — I had such an amazing time! It was great to catch up after so long, and your family made me feel really welcome.

I especially enjoyed our walk in the countryside on Saturday morning. The views were incredible, and the picnic you prepared was delicious! I also loved the film night — we should definitely do that again.

Thanks again for letting me stay. Everything was so comfortable, and you really went out of your way to make me feel at home. Next time, you must come and visit me — I’ll make sure you’re treated just as well!
Hope everything’s going well at work. Let’s plan our next weekend together soon!
Take care,
**Sophie**

plan: ### Paragraph 2 – Description of food and service
• Describe typical dishes – grilled fish, espetada, fresh bread
• Mention quality, presentation, and speed of service
• Staff are helpful and make you feel at home
### Paragraph 3 – Atmosphere and value
• Rustic decoration and live folk music in the evenings
• Prices reasonable for the quality
• Ideal for families or small groups
text: **When it comes to choosing** a traditional restaurant in Madeira, the number of options can be overwhelming. Nevertheless, O Lagar stands out as a great choice for authentic island cuisine. Located in Câmara de Lobos, O Lagar has been a favourite among tourists and locals for over thirty years.

**Regarded as one of the best** traditional restaurants in the region, few can rival its quality and authenticity. The menu features regional specialities such as grilled fish, “espetada”, meat on skewer, and homemade bread with garlic butter.

**The thing that is most likely to impress you is the exceptional** quality and speed of service. The other feature which I found most impressive is the staff’s knowledge — they always recommend the perfect local wine.

**If you happen to appreciate** live music, the folk performances on weekends are by far the most atmospheric I have experienced. By far the best feature is its welcoming atmosphere that makes you feel at home. Prices are reasonable considering the quality, making it ideal for families.
**For anyone who is interested in** authentic Madeiran cuisine, this is a must. I can assure you that O Lagar will leave a lasting impression.

**Choosing the right social media platform is never easy**, but Instagram definitely deserves your attention if you enjoy visual creativity. Known for its photo-sharing features, Instagram has been a favourite among teenagers and young adults worldwide. Regarded as one of the best social networking apps available, few can compete with its simplicity and creative possibilities.

**What impresses me most is** how easy it is to use. You can upload content instantly and discover inspiring ideas from around the world. The other feature which I found most impressive is the Stories function, which lets you share temporary moments.
**Anyone interested in photography will be especially impressed** by the professional filters and editing tools.

**By far the best aspect of Instagram** is its ability to connect people through visual experiences, whether following friends or educational accounts. However, some drawbacks exist. Users can spend excessive time scrolling instead of being productive. Additionally, content isn’t always authentic, creating pressure to look perfect.
This is a platform **which you cannot afford to miss** for its creative possibilities. I guarantee it will not disappoint anyone seeking connection — but moderation is essential.

text: ### Introduction

**The main objective of this report is to assess** the current school facilities and suggest improvements. The information presented in this report was collected through a questionnaire conducted among students.
### Current Situation

**It is generally agreed** that the school provides a pleasant learning environment. What makes the library so valuable is that it offers a wide selection of books and resources. By far the best aspect of the facilities is the sports hall, which is modern and well-equipped.
### Problems

However, **one major concern expressed by students** is the outdated computer equipment. By far the worst aspect of the IT facilities is that machines frequently break down, taking into account that students rely on them for coursework. The library is far from ideal since it lacks sufficient seating during exam periods. This is mainly due to the fact that student numbers have increased significantly.
### Recommendations

**One key recommendation would be to** replace outdated computers with modern equipment. In order to maximize study space, I would strongly recommend adding more library seating. It is essential that the school invests in covered outdoor areas.
### Conclusion

Taking everything into account**, it seems clear that targeted improvements would significantly enhance** the learning environment. To sum up, the findings clearly show that students would benefit greatly from these changes.
### Introduction
**This report aims to provide a summary of** my recent two-week exchange programme in Spain. **The findings in this report are drawn from** interviews and feedback obtained during the visit.
### Accommodation and School Life

**It was generally felt by all participants that** the host families were exceptionally welcoming. What made the accommodation so successful was that families encouraged constant Spanish practice. By far the best aspect of the school was the teaching approach, which combined traditional lessons with cultural activities. Many visitors referred to the staff support as the most impressive feature.
### Activities and Learning

**The highlight of the exchange was** the visit to local museums and historical sites. One positive aspect of the excursions is that they allowed participants to practise language skills in authentic contexts. What makes these experiences so valuable is that students gain confidence through real communication.
### Recommendations

**One key recommendation would be to** organize more group activities between Spanish and visiting students. In order to improve preparation, I would strongly recommend providing language lessons before departure. It is essential that participants receive information about local customs in advance.
### Conclusion

**The main conclusion to be drawn is that** such experiences provide invaluable language practice. Taking everything into account, **I strongly recommend that** other students participate in future programmes.
